evals.name: client-facing-tiny-project
evals.prompt: I'm about to email this tiny Specflow project to a new client before a demo call tomorrow. I want a single browsable HTML page they can double-click open — showing all the specs, status, acceptance criteria, and dependencies — so they can see exactly what we're building and what will be verified. The project is at .claude/skills/spec-viewer/evals/fixtures/tiny-project/ and already has a test-results.json sitting next to .specflow/specs/. Please produce the deliverable and tell me exactly what file to send them.
evals.expected_output: A single self-contained specs.html file at the tiny-project root, generated by running the spec-viewer skill's build script. Output should include all 6 dev specs, test results overlay, and a summary printed back. Folder-overview coverage line should appear in the summary even though the fixture has none.

evals.name: implicit-trigger-presentation
evals.prompt: We're presenting the BERD project to a new partner on Wednesday and I want to show them everything we've specified so far — domains, capabilities, acceptance criteria, the lot. Not a ppt deck, more like something they can browse themselves during and after the call. I have 100-ish spec files under .specflow/specs/ in this repo. What's the quickest way to hand them something polished?
evals.expected_output: Skill should trigger from the implicit phrasing ('show them everything we've specified', 'something they can browse themselves', 'polished'). Should generate specs.html at the BERD repo root and describe how to send it. If .specflow/specs-business/ exists at the BERD root, the viewer should default to the Business toggle.

evals.name: regenerate-with-test-results
evals.prompt: Hey, we just ran the latest Vitest suite on the tiny-project fixture (under .claude/skills/spec-viewer/evals/fixtures/tiny-project/) and the results are already in test-results.json alongside .specflow/specs/. Can you regenerate the spec documentation page so the client sees the fresh pass/fail status on each acceptance criterion? Put the output at dist/specs.html this time instead of the root.
evals.expected_output: Regenerated specs.html at dist/specs.html under tiny-project/ with 11 test results overlay (pass/fail/skip badges), using the spec-viewer skill's --out flag.

evals.name: folder-overview-rendered-as-node
evals.prompt: I just added an _overview.md to the alpha/ domain folder in the tiny-project fixture explaining what alpha is for. Can you regenerate the spec viewer and confirm the alpha folder is now clickable in the sidebar and that clicking it shows the overview content in the right pane? Project root: .claude/skills/spec-viewer/evals/fixtures/tiny-project/.
evals.expected_output: Build script should be run, _overview.md under alpha/ should be parsed and emitted into the SPEC_DATA payload (under trees.dev.overviews with folder_path 'alpha'), and the rendered template should treat the folder as a clickable node whose right-pane view shows the overview body. Summary line 'dev folder overviews: N/M written' should reflect the new file. The agent should create the _overview.md if it doesn't exist before regenerating, or describe the expected payload shape if it can't write to the fixture.

evals.name: default-tab-is-business-when-both-trees-present
evals.prompt: I just split the tiny-project fixture into two trees — there's now a .specflow/specs-business/ alongside .specflow/specs/. When I open the generated HTML I want stakeholders to land on the Business view, not the Developer view, since the deck is for a non-technical audience. Make sure that's how it'll behave and regenerate the page.
evals.expected_output: Agent should set up a sibling .specflow/specs-business/ directory under the fixture (at minimum a single _index.md or one *.business.md leaf so the tree is detected), regenerate the viewer, and confirm via the summary that 'business specs' appears with a non-zero count. The default_tree field in the SPEC_DATA payload should be 'business' (and the agent should mention this default behaviour explicitly in its response).

evals.name: business-to-dev-navigation-via-implemented-by
evals.prompt: On the business spec page for our 'signup' outcome, I want stakeholders to be able to click straight through to the developer spec(s) that implement it. Walk me through how that works in the generated viewer and verify the cross-link is live in the payload after running the build. The fixture is at .claude/skills/spec-viewer/evals/fixtures/tiny-project/ — feel free to add a minimal business spec with implemented_by: [alpha.onboarding] if the fixture doesn't have one yet.
evals.expected_output: Agent should ensure a business spec exists with implemented_by listing alpha.onboarding (creating one in .specflow/specs-business/ if needed), regenerate, and verify both that the business spec's payload has 'implemented_by' populated AND that the dev spec alpha.onboarding has 'implements' auto-completed (back-link reconciliation). Should describe the UI flow: clicking the chip in the 'Implemented by' section switches the toggle to Developer view and navigates to the dev spec.

evals.name: dev-to-business-navigation-via-implements
evals.prompt: Same fixture (.claude/skills/spec-viewer/evals/fixtures/tiny-project/) — the alpha.billing dev spec serves a billing business outcome. I want the dev spec page to show an 'Implements' section that links back to that business spec. Set this up in the fixture if needed and regenerate. Confirm the dev spec's frontmatter implements: ... is reflected in the payload and renders as clickable chips.
evals.expected_output: Agent should add 'implements: [<biz-id>]' to alpha.billing's frontmatter (or create the matching business spec if missing), regenerate, and verify the dev spec's payload entry has 'implements' populated. Should describe that the rendered Implements section will link back to the business spec by switching the tree toggle and navigating.

evals.name: unmapped-badge-on-dev-spec-without-implements
evals.prompt: I want a clear visual flag in the spec viewer for any dev spec that hasn't been mapped to a business outcome yet — the team needs to see at a glance which capabilities are missing the link. We have .specflow/specs-business/ alive in the tiny-project fixture but only some dev specs declare implements:. Run the viewer and tell me how many dev specs come up as unmapped, and how the badge surfaces.
evals.expected_output: Agent should ensure both trees exist under the fixture (creating a minimal business spec if needed), regenerate, and the build summary should print 'unmapped dev specs (no `implements:`): N' with N > 0 when at least one dev spec lacks implements. Should describe that the rendered viewer shows an 'Unmapped' badge in the sidebar leaf and in the spec header for those specs, and that the Spec Health panel rolls them up. The 'unmapped: ...' warning should appear in the warnings array.

evals.name: search-matches-folder-overview-text
evals.prompt: Quick sanity check on the search in the generated HTML — if I add an _overview.md under .specflow/specs/alpha/ that contains the phrase 'authentication flows' (even though no spec.md mentions authentication) and then I type 'authentication' in the search bar, will it surface the alpha folder node? I want overview text to be searchable, not just spec content. Fixture at .claude/skills/spec-viewer/evals/fixtures/tiny-project/.
evals.expected_output: Agent should write an _overview.md containing 'authentication flows' to .specflow/specs/alpha/ in the fixture, regenerate, and confirm by inspecting the SPEC_DATA payload that the overview body is present (under trees.dev.overviews['alpha'].body) AND describe that the template's search index includes overview body text alongside spec content. Should explicitly note that searching 'authentication' will match this overview even though no spec.md contains the word.

evals.name: sidebar-subtitle-is-first-sentence-of-overview
evals.prompt: When I open the generated HTML I want each folder in the sidebar to show a one-line subtitle underneath its name — the first sentence of its _overview.md — so clients can read the tree as a map without having to click into every node. Verify this works on the tiny-project fixture (.claude/skills/spec-viewer/evals/fixtures/tiny-project/) and tell me what subtitle the alpha folder will display.
evals.expected_output: Agent should ensure .specflow/specs/alpha/_overview.md exists with a clear one-sentence opening (e.g., 'Alpha covers core onboarding and billing flows.'), regenerate, and verify by inspecting the payload that trees.dev.overviews['alpha'].summary is non-empty and equals the first sentence of the body (skipping headings/lists). Should report the exact subtitle string back.
